The Prohibitionist Internet Strategy:
www.we-can-lie-louder-than-you-can-tell-the-truth.con
Analysis By Richard Cowan

Just when I thought I was getting used to the cynicism of the Drug Czar and the Partnership For a Marijuana-Free America, they have outdone themselves with a new national media campaign promoting their new prohibitionist propaganda site, www.theantidrug.com.

The print ads may be even worse than the site itself. They are a part of the new policy of paying the media to lie to the people, which they have long done for free. The general concept is to sell the new marijuana prohibition.

See
Drug Czar Brags About The Entertainment Industry and The Media Prostituting Themselves
For Prohibitionist Propaganda  -- 2 Items
and links

This is a fuzzy lovable new program that emphasizes family conversations, which in this context means conning parents into lying to their children, thereby undermining both parental authority and the credibility of "drug education." This will have the effect of encouraging hard drug use and increasing arrests, which is in the interest of the prohibitionists’ constituency.
See
The Washington Post Says That Parents Should Tell Children The Truth
And Provides Them With The Lies To Use While They Are Doing It.

The worst feature of the print ads is the headline, variously, "Truth," "Love," or "Honesty" followed by lies, hatred, and dishonesty.
See
The 50th Anniversary of The Publishing Of Orwell’s 1984
Analysis By Richard Cowan

Consider the ad headed with "Honesty." It was in a full-page ad in Newsweek magazine as well as other publications. It is accompanied by a what appears to be a greatly magnified picture of a marijuana flower. The caption reads:

"This is where THC comes from. THC is the active ingredient in marijuana. It looks the same today as it did in 1960. The difference is how much of it is in marijuana today. Pot today is often grown hydroponically and genetically altered to produce more THC in each plant. The production of marijuana is a commercial industry that in many ways has created a drug which is much different than it was in the 1970’s."

All that under the heading – "Honesty."

First, there is no data on marijuana potency from the 1960s.
Second, according to NIDA the average potency is still around 3%, and the --sometimes hydroponically grown -- sinsemilla is around 7%.

  • "Most ordinary marijuana has an average of 3 percent THC.

  • Sinsemilla (made from just the buds and flowering tops of female plants) has an average of 7.5 percent THC, with a range as high as 24 percent.

  • Hashish (the sticky resin from the female plant flowers) has an average of 3.6 percent, with a range as high as 28 percent.

  • Hash oil, a tar-like liquid distilled from hashish, has an average of 16 percent, with a range as high as 43 percent."

From http://www.nida.nih.gov/MarijBroch/parentpg3-4N.html

See
The American Academy of Pediatrics To Embrace "Potent Pot" Line:
Party Line Takes Precedence Over Caring For Children.
Medical and Journalistic Malpractice
and links

In other words, the government’s own data do not show that marijuana is significantly different, and certainly not more dangerous.

Notice also the new line that marijuana has been "genetically altered." Any plant that has been crossed with another has been "genetically altered." This has been going on for centuries, but in the context of modern science this might be taken to mean that it has been "genetically engineered" – i.e. that the plants' genes have been directly altered. That seems to be the implication here.

Once when I was National Director of NORML I called Steve Dnistrian, the chief propagandist for the Partnership, to challenge them on an ad that implied that marijuana was responsible for how violent the world is today – in contrast to the sixties. His response was simply that they did not explicitly say that marijuana was responsible for the violence. Well, they did not explicitly say that marijuana is being genetically engineered.

There is a level of cynicism working here that is difficult to comprehend.

The footer on the ad says,
"Smoking marijuana is harmful. The younger you are the more harmful it is. Research has shown that people who smoke marijuana before the age of 15 are 7 times more likely to use other drugs than people who don’t smoke marijuana. Studies also show that people who did not smoke marijuana by the time that they were 21 were more likely to never smoke marijuana."
Of course, this is just the "Gateway Theory" and it is not the result of "research" or "studies," but simply correlations inferred from surveys.
See
"Those who insist on keeping the plant illegal bear a serious degree of moral responsibility for young marijuana users who do go on to use cocaine, heroin, PCP or other genuinely dangerous or addictive drugs."
Alan Bock, of the Orange County Register On the Real Gateway

In these ads, they are lying to parents to get them to lie to children in the name of Love, Honesty and Truth. My word for all of this would also be very simple, Evil.

Below is their version Truth.

TRUTH THE ANTI-DRUG

The most effective deterrent to drug use among kids isn't the police, or prisons, or politicians. One of the most effective deterrents to drug use among kids is their parents. Kids who learn about the risks of drugs from their parents are 36% less likely to smoke marijuana than kids who learn nothing from them. They are 50% less likely to use inhalants. 56% less likely to use cocaine. 65% less likely to use LSD. So if you're a parent, talk to your kids about drugs. Research also shows that 74% of all fourth graders wish their parents would talk to them about drugs. If you don't know what to say, call 800-788-2800 or visit www.theantidrug.com.

We can help you.

The Geocentric System

Five hundred years ago, the sun was thought to revolve around the earth. People did not know then what we know now. Truths change. We now know smoking marijuana is harmful.
